sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Hamtramck?
sections.html:
Hamtramck is a two-square-mile city in Wayne County that sits almost entirely inside Detroit's borders, so a sale here follows Hamtramck's own city code and Wayne County's tax process rather than anything Detroit does. You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take an as-is cash purchase, and each route runs into the same three local checkpoints: the city's pre-sale inspection rules, the treasurer's tax calendar, and the assessor's transfer paperwork.

The city covers 2.09 square miles, all of it land, and Interstate 75 runs roughly along its western edge with I-94 near the southern edge. Downtown Detroit is about 5 miles south. The Census Bureau estimates 27,261 residents for July 1, 2025, down 4.1 percent from the 2020 estimates base, which tells you the market is small and house-by-house rather than a growth-driven one.

sections.h2: How did Hamtramck's housing stock come about?
sections.html:
Most of the older homes trace back to the factory boom. The Dodge Brothers plant opened in 1914, and Hamtramck's population jumped by more than 1,200 percent between 1910 and 1920 as workers moved close to the line. The village became a city in 1922, partly to resist annexation by Detroit. By the middle of the 1920s, Wikipedia's history notes, roughly 78 percent of residents owned or were buying their homes.

That history explains what a buyer walks into today: compact lots, frame houses and flats built close together, and many decades of owners making their own repairs. Polish families gave way over time to immigrants from Yemen, Bangladesh, Pakistan and the Balkans, and a 2018 survey found schoolchildren speaking 16 native languages. Houses that changed hands inside one family for generations often carry unrecorded repairs, old liens or unclear titles, which is worth sorting out before you set a price.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Hamtramck homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 Census figures show a city that looks different from the rest of Michigan. Use them to set expectations, then rely on a local comparison for your own street.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $131,000.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 58.3 percent, across 7,120 households.
  • Persons per household: 3.86, which points to large households and heavily used kitchens and baths.
  • Median gross rent: $989.
  • Foreign-born residents: 46.7 percent; 73.5 percent speak a language other than English at home.

Because of those household sizes, a house with extra bedrooms or a finished basement often draws more interest than the same square footage elsewhere. Say plainly in your listing or conversation which rooms are legal bedrooms.

sections.h2: Does Hamtramck require an inspection before I sell?
sections.html:
Only for some owners. Under the city's pre-sale subchapter (sections 150.201 to 150.206), a property that holds a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate cannot be transferred, and no one may act as broker for the transfer, without a current certificate of approval from the Building Department. Everyone else may request a voluntary inspection, but once you file that request you cannot withdraw it, and every violation found must be fixed to earn the certificate.

The same code gives you a way through if repairs would delay closing. The city will not accept a property transfer affidavit for an NEZ home without the certificate, unless the buyer signs a notarized affidavit promising to fix the listed violations within six months. A few more details matter:

  • An inspection report is valid for one year, and a certificate of approval lasts one year from issue.
  • If the building official sees serious neglect or hazards, a mandatory inspection can be ordered whatever the NEZ status.
  • The certificate is not a warranty. The city disclaims liability for hidden defects, mold and asbestos.

Ask the Hamtramck Building Department whether your parcel carries an NEZ certificate before you sign a purchase agreement.

sections.h2: What if the house is vacant, foreclosed or a rental?
sections.html:
Chapter 96 of the city code treats foreclosed and long-empty houses differently. A residential property unoccupied for 180 days or longer needs a certificate of occupancy before anyone moves in, and so does any property foreclosed by a bank, county or other holder, whatever the length of vacancy. To get the certificate the applicant must pass inspection, correct violations and clear all previously billed property taxes, special assessments, water and sewer bills and city cleanup charges.

Rentals follow Chapter 150. A non-owner-occupied dwelling needs a certificate of compliance, issued for two years at first and three years on later renewals. The city code says a sale ends the certificate immediately, and the new owner must apply for a fresh one within 30 days of the transfer. If you own a rental and have received a notice of violation, you must give the buyer a copy and file a notarized acknowledgment of it with the building official before you sell or convey the property, land contracts included.

sections.h2: When are Hamtramck property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Hamtramck bills summer taxes on July 1 and winter taxes on December 1, and the city treasurer collects them first. Unpaid balances move to the Wayne County Treasurer on March 1, where interest and fees grow quickly. The table summarizes the sequence for a parcel that goes unpaid.

Hamtramck and Wayne County tax calendar for an unpaid parcel
StageWhat happens
July 1Summer bill issued; due in full by August 20, or half in July and the balance by December 30
December 1Winter bill issued; due by February 15
February 28Last day to pay the city
March 1Delinquent taxes go to Wayne County with a 4 percent administration fee and 1 percent monthly interest
March 1, a year after thatParcel forfeits; $175 fee added and interest rises to 1.5 percent monthly
March 31 and April 1, a year after forfeitureJudgment of foreclosure; title passes to the county treasurer unless paid

Source: Hamtramck Treasurer and Wayne County Treasurer timeline pages. Foreclosed homes are then offered at public auction in September and October, so a seller with two years of arrears has a hard deadline.

sections.h2: What paperwork does the assessor need after a Hamtramck sale?
sections.html:
The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the assessor within 45 days of the transfer, or the city can charge $5 per day up to $200. The seller should sign a Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption so the old claim comes off the parcel; skipping the rescission can create a bill later if the state audits the exemption. Buyers who will live in the house sign a new exemption affidavit, which removes 18 mills of school operating tax.

Michigan also resets the taxable value after a sale. Under MCL 211.27a, the year after a transfer, taxable value becomes the state equalized value (about half of market value), so a buyer's first bill after closing can run higher than yours did. Appeals of an assessment go to the March Board of Review.

sections.h2: What does recording and transfer tax cost on a Hamtramck sale?
sections.html:
The seller owes Michigan's state real estate transfer tax of $3.75 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.525), plus a county tax under MCL 207.504 of 55 cents per $500 in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 residents and up to 75 cents in a larger one. Both are paid to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed, and they apply when the deed is recorded with the Wayne County Register of Deeds.

Transfers to a child, stepchild, grandchild or adopted child are exempt, as are court-ordered transfers without a stated price and deeds given in foreclosure of government-backed loans (MCL 207.526). Ask the Wayne County Register of Deeds which county rate applies and what recording fee to add.

sections.h2: Does Hamtramck have a local income tax I should plan for?
sections.html: Yes. Hamtramck is one of the Michigan cities with its own income tax, at 1.00 percent for residents and 0.50 percent for nonresidents. Ask the city income tax office how a move out of town or rental income affects your filing.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of approval to sell my Hamtramck house?
faqs.a: Only if the property holds a Neighborhood Enterprise Zone certificate. Other owners may request a voluntary inspection, but a request cannot be withdrawn once filed. A buyer can sign a notarized affidavit promising to correct violations within six months in place of a certificate.

faqs.q: When is the Hamtramck summer tax bill due?
faqs.a: August 20. The city bills on July 1, and paying half in July pushes the balance to December 30. Winter bills are due February 15, and delinquent balances move to Wayne County on March 1.

faqs.q: How long can taxes go unpaid before Hamtramck property is foreclosed?
faqs.a: About two years. Taxes go delinquent on March 1, the parcel forfeits a year later, and a circuit court judgment of foreclosure follows another year after the delinquency date. Owners can still redeem by paying all taxes, interest and fees by March 31 of the foreclosure year.

faqs.q: What forms follow a Hamtramck closing?
faqs.a: The buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit within 45 days, and the seller files a rescission of the principal residence exemption. The buyer files a new exemption affidavit if the home will be a principal residence.

faqs.q: Does a rental certificate transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The city ends a non-owner-occupied certificate on sale, and the new owner must apply for a new one within 30 days after the transfer of ownership.
